title: Flourless Chocolate Torte
description: A dense, fudgy chocolate cake made with no flour, just chocolate, butter, sugar, eggs and a little cocoa. Serve it in thin slices with a dusting of cocoa or a spoonful of softly whipped cream.
notes:
The torte puffs in the oven and sinks a little as it cools; a few cracks on top are normal and the cocoa covers them.

It keeps for 4 days, covered, in the fridge and is best brought back to room temperature for 30 minutes before serving. Slice with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry.

Naturally gluten-free if the chocolate and cocoa are; check the labels if that matters.
ingredients: 10 ounces (285 g) bittersweet chocolate (60 to 70%), chopped
3/4 cup (170 g) unsalted butter, cubed, plus more for the pan
1/3 cup (30 g) unsweetened cocoa powder, plus more for dusting
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) with a rack in the middle. Butter a 9-inch (23 cm) springform pan and line the base with a round of parchment.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, or in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring until smooth.
Whisk in the sugar, salt, vanilla and espresso powder. Let the mixture cool for 5 minutes, until warm rather than hot.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each, until the batter is thick and glossy. Sift the cocoa over the top and fold it in until no dry streaks remain.

Scrape into the pan and smooth the top. Bake until the top has a thin, dull crust, the edges are set and the centre wobbles only slightly when you nudge the pan, 30 to 35 minutes. A toothpick pushed in 2 inches from the edge should come out with moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan on a rack for at least 1 hour. Run a thin knife around the edge and remove the ring.
Whip the cream and sugar to soft peaks. Dust the torte with cocoa through a fine sieve and serve in slices with the cream.
